audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (final): primary final stress kept as the dominant/citation-form pattern, not in the strict set, with a note that accent is lexically penult in a minority of words (b'idʌd 'we', m'onʌd, t'ɛndʌ, qur'unɪ; Weiers 2003 'seldom on the penult') and morphologically constant on the stem-final/connective vowel in present-tense verb forms (in'ʌnʌmbi 'I laugh', ʌtʃʌr'unʌ 'brings') and on the negator in negative imperatives (b'iboɪʀʌ), i.e. non-final in the word.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Source quality is not the problem: Weiers 1972 is the authoritative first-hand grammar and the quotation is verbatim at p.89-90. The problem is that the record codes 'fixed-strict' (final at every length, counts as exceptionless (the strict set)) while the deciding passage itself says the accent position is 'frei-konstant', lists 'Seltener Paroxytona' and 'Sporadisch Proparoxytona' with examples, gives further non-final-accent words on the same page (sec. 2B: [dʒ'ʌn:ʌtu] 'Paradies', [t'ɛn:ɪ] 'ihn', [m'ut:ʌ] 'ebendort'), and states (p.89-90) that in verbal inflection the accent sits constantly on the verb-stem ultima or connective vowel ([in'ʌnʌmdʌ] 'wir lachen', antepenult of the word) and on the negation in negative imperatives. Weiers 2003:252 ('mainly on the last syllable, seldom on the penult'; pitch on stem-final/connective vowel in the narrative present, e.g. inanambi) says the same; Ligeti 1955b:145,150 (fetc

sources.quote: "The position of this centralizing accent is free-constant. The freedom of the accent emerges from the following: most of the words, which consist predominantly of two, occasionally of three or more stem syllables, can be: 1. Mostly oxytones [final-stressed], e.g. ... 2. More rarely paroxytones [penult-stressed], e.g. ... 3. Sporadically proparoxytones [antepenult-stressed], these being mostly compound words."

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p.145: 'Dans le moghol, l'accent ne tombe pas sur la syllabe initiale, comme dans la plupart des langues mongoles ; cette langue se conforme totalement aux règles d'accentuation des langues tadjik environnantes.' p.150: in Leech's notation 'l'î ne marque pas toujours la longueur mais souvent l'accent, comme par exemple dans les mots barîna, khagîna' (penult accent on the stem-final vowel of finite verb forms, matching Weiers's 'Konstanz' in verbal inflection).
